subject: Copywriting
title: Edward Bernays: The Father of PR
description: A fast breakdown of Edward Bernays: The Father of PR for builders.

hook.text: Edward Bernays, Freud's nephew, called propaganda 'the engineering of consent.' He made it respectable—and renamed it.

buildup.text: In 1929, Bernays staged 'Torches of Freedom'—women smoking in an Easter parade—to sell cigarettes as liberation.

discovery.text: He didn't advertise cigarettes. He advertised freedom. The product was irrelevant; the symbol was irresistible.

twist.text: Bernays proved that selling ideas is more powerful than selling products.

climax.text: His 1928 book 'Propaganda' argued that invisible rulers shape public opinion. He was both warning and teaching.

punchline.text: Freud's nephew sold cigarettes as freedom. He called it public relations.

quiz.question: What did Bernays call his 1929 campaign for women smoking?

details.summary: Edward Bernays, Sigmund Freud's nephew, essentially invented public relations by applying psychological principles to mass persuasion. His 1928 book 'Propaganda' argued that invisible manipulation of public opinion is essential to democracy — a controversial claim that shaped modern advertising.
details.whyItMatters: Bernays created the playbook that advertisers, politicians, and PR professionals still follow. Understanding his methods reveals the psychological architecture behind most modern persuasion campaigns.
takeaways: Bernays applied Freud's theories of the unconscious to mass marketing
He staged the 'Torches of Freedom' campaign linking smoking to feminism
His work blurred the line between information and manipulation

faq.question: What was Bernays's most famous campaign?
faq.answer: The 1929 'Torches of Freedom' campaign, where he hired women to smoke cigarettes during the Easter Parade, framing smoking as a feminist act. It doubled the female cigarette market and demonstrated how emotional associations could override rational objections.

faq.question: How did Bernays differ from earlier propagandists?
faq.answer: Bernays was the first to systematically apply psychology to persuasion at scale. Rather than simply repeating messages, he engineered events and cultural associations that made people feel they were making free choices while being guided toward predetermined conclusions.
